title: Adults with Special Needs who are Financially-dependent on Retired Parents
what_it_is: Adults with Special Needs who are Financially-dependent on Retired Parents

sections.label: Resident employment rate for PwDs
sections.summary: The average resident employment rate for PwDs aged 15 to 64 rose from 28.2% in 2018 to 2019 to 31.4% in 2021 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Based on the Comprehensive Labour Force Survey, the average resident employment rate for PwDs aged 15 to 64 has increased steadily from 28.2% in the period of 2018 to 2019 when data on PwDs was first collected, to 31.4% in 2021 to 2022.

sections.label: SG Enable job placements
sections.summary: Between 2020 and 2022, SG Enable and its partners placed an average of 500 PwDs into jobs each year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Between 2020 and 2022, SG Enable and its partners placed an average of 500 PwDs into jobs each year.

sections.label: EEC wage support
sections.summary: The EEC provides up to 20% wage support for employees with disabilities earning below $4,000 per month, capped at $400.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The EEC provides up to 20% wage support for employees with disabilities earning below $4,000 per month, capped at $400.

sections.label: EBH training and 40% target
sections.summary: The EBH will provide more customised skills training and job coaching, and partners are encouraged to help raise the PwD employment rate to 40% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The EBH will provide more customised skills training and job coaching to help PwDs remain in their jobs and also open up opportunities in new sectors such as logistics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We encourage partners across the private, people and public sectors to join our efforts to achieve the aspirational target to raise the employment rate of PwDs to 40% by 2030.

sections.label: Business hubs and inclusive industries
sections.summary: More business hubs will be set up to bring employment and support services closer to PwDs and caregivers, and other industries amenable to disability inclusive employment will be looked at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: More business hubs will be set up across the island so that we can bring employment services and support services closer to where PwDs and their caregivers live.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: In terms of how we want to achieve our aspirational target of getting 40% employment rates for PwDs by 2030, another strategy is to look at which other industries are more amenable to disability inclusive employment.

sections.label: Conversation on disability financial data
sections.summary: The speaker says the conversation on these issues must be pushed further and that Ms Carrie Tan's request to track data on the financial situation of adults with disabilities has some merit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I think we do need to initiate a conversation around these issues – not that we have not already, but we need to push the conversation even further so that we can drive this cause to a maximal effect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I do think that the hon Member Ms Carrie Tan's request to track data on the financial situation of adults with disabilities has some merit.

sections.label: Segmentation of archetypes for financial security
sections.summary: The speaker calls for better segmentation of archetypes to ensure financial security for this sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Ms Phua, can you get to your supplementary question?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: So, I think that there should be a better way of segmentation of these archetypes so that better methods in ensuring financial security can come about for this particular sector.
